subject: Streamflow: request for SLA exceptions on streaming vs sync endpoints
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan@streamflow.ai>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: SLA clarifications for streaming endpoints (RFP section 4.2)

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked very promising. Our procurement team sent over a short set of SLA clarifications tied to streaming vs polling endpoints (attached as 'Streamflow_RFP_SLA_questions.pdf'). Two items are flagged as blocking for our security/compliance review:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) measurement methodology: we need a clear definition and measurement window.
2) Token emission (tokens/sec) guarantee during sustained bursts and the carveouts for preemption/fallback to non-streaming endpoints.

Can Redwood provide example contract language or acceptable exception language for both? Also please confirm if there are documented fallback behavior and observable metrics we can reference in the SOW.

Evan Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Streamflow AI
procurement@streamflow.ai

Attachment: Streamflow_RFP_SLA_questions.pdf (pdf)
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Evan Liu <evan@streamflow.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for streaming endpoints (RFP section 4.2)

Evan —

Appreciate the notes and the clear ask. Looping in Kim and Aditya for the technical and legal framing. High-level answers up front:

- We can provide explicit TTFT language measured at the 95th percentile over rolling 5-minute windows per endpoint and per region, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and customer-triggered load tests.
- For token emission we can commit to sustained token/sec baselines per reserved capacity tier and define fallbacks to a compatible non-streaming endpoint if the streaming pool is fully preempted.

I'll follow up with suggested contract text and a short appendix that explains collection points for metrics (client-observed vs server-measured).

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

> Rafael / Evan — adding details below that I think will cover the RFP ask and make the exceptions concrete.
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for streaming endpoints (RFP section 4.2)

Evan / team —

Below is proposed language and operational notes you can drop into the SOW or contract appendix. I've separated the hard commit language from recommended operational carveouts so the procurement team can see explicit obligations vs expected behavior under edge conditions.

--- Proposed SLA language (draft) ---
1) Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) Commitment
   - Definition: TTFT is defined as the elapsed time from request receipt by the Redwood ingress to the delivery of the first token byte to the client via the streaming connection.
   - Measurement: TTFT will be measured at the 95th percentile over rolling 5-minute windows, aggregated per endpoint and per region. Scheduled maintenance windows and customer-initiated replay/load tests are excluded from measurement.
   - Target: 95th percentile TTFT <= 220 ms for requests under 2k input tokens on the Dedicated tier.

2) Token Emission / Sustained Throughput
   - Definition: Sustained token rate is the mean tokens/second delivered for a request after the first token, excluding natural model-side generation pauses.
   - Commitment: For reserved capacity plans we commit to sustained delivery baselines (e.g., Tier A: >= 120 tokens/sec; Tier B: >= 60 tokens/sec), measured as a 1-minute moving average at the server egress.

3) Fallback and Graceful Degradation
   - If streaming pools are temporarily unable to meet committed sustained rates (e.g., due to preemption or catastrophic hardware failure), Redwood will:
     a) Route new traffic to a compatible non-streaming endpoint that returns a complete response with an explicit indication that the response was served via non-streaming fallback.
     b) Notify the customer via the Console and by e-mail within 15 minutes of observed degradation in the affected region.

--- Operational carveouts (non-contractual guidance) ---
- Preemption carveout: transient preemption of preemptible nodes for less than 2 minutes is considered a recoverable event and not a breach if fallback took effect.
- Model-side stalls: when the underlying model requires additional compute for a single request, token emission can be interrupted; these events will be visible as spikes in model compute latency and will be reported in the incident postmortem.

Attachments: I can also produce a short appendix that maps the console metrics (ingress latency, first-token, server-egress-rate) to the contractual metrics.

Kim Park
Senior Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, Evan Liu <evan@streamflow.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA clarifications for streaming endpoints (RFP section 4.2)

Adding a couple practical recommendations from an operational standpoint:

- Canary periods: include a 30-day canary for new regions or model variants where TTFT is monitored but not subject to monetary SLA credits (report-only). This reduces false positives during ramp.
- Observable hooks: recommend the contract reference three console metrics with sample query strings so Streamflow can verify claims in real time (we'll include exact PromQL/SQL snippets in the appendix).
- Pricing note: sustained token/sec guarantees on Dedicated tiers increase reservation costs by ~8-12% in our pricing ladder; we should flag this in the commercial term sheet.

If you want, I can draft the fallback language that the infra team can wire into endpoint routing so the route tagging is consistent with the contract wording.

- Aditya
Principal Product, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Evan —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short SOW appendix and proposed SLA paragraph that pulls in Kim and Aditya's language (file: redwood-proposed-sla-v1.docx). Key callouts:

- Clear TTFT definition + measurement window (95th pct, 5m rolling).
- Sustained token/sec commitments for Dedicated tiers and explicit fallback behavior to a non-streaming endpoint (with event notification).
- Canary/reporting period for new regions, and a pricing uplift note tied to sustained-rate guarantees.

If that looks good I'd propose a quick 30-min call next week to agree on carveouts and confirm the DocuSign-ready version.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
